deletion_attack.attack: delete one kill criterion from a copy of capture_template.json, then check whether the pre-registration completeness check fires
deletion_attack.conclusion: No mechanism anywhere in this corpus fires when a whole, well-formed kill criterion ('pot_life_below_90_min', method 'ASTM D562 KU-vs-time...', already axis-A-passing on its own) is deleted from capture_template.json: axis A (methods-named) only validates gates that ARE present, so its pass/fail verdict AND its exact missing-gates list are BYTE-IDENTICAL between the 7-gate original and the 6-gate mutated copy -- the boolean and the list carry zero information about the deletion either way. Axis B confirms (again) that no content-hash lock field exists anywhere to pin the SET of required kill gates the way falsification_protocol.json's locked_rank_hash pins the barrier rank (hash_matches=True there, but nothing analogous for early_kill_gates/acceptance_gates). The pre-registration completeness check the claim assumes exists DOES NOT FIRE on this deletion.
deletion_attack.deleted_gate_kill_if: mixed material fails 90 min sprayable/KU window at 73F

finding: CLAIM_REFUTED. Of the 5 axes the done_criterion names, 2 fail on the REAL, unmodified corpus (no planted defect needed): (axis_b) acceptance thresholds and kill criteria are NOT locked before measurement the way the barrier rank is -- falsification_protocol.json's locked_rank_hash IS a real, recomputed content hash (hash_matches=True), but no equivalent lock field exists anywhere for early_kill_gates/acceptance_gates in capture_template.json; and (axis_d) uncertainty is explicitly point-only -- falsification_protocol.json's own uncertainty_status field states 'no calibrated uncertainty available', and the one place a quantification would live, statistical_decision_rules.power_analysis_path ('out/power_analysis.json'), is a dangling reference to a file that does not exist anywhere in the module. The literal attack (delete gate 'gel_or_phase_split' from a copy of capture_template.json) confirms axis_b's absence is not just theoretical: the deletion goes completely undetected by every check this corpus can run on itself, because nothing pins the SET of required kill gates -- only the shape of gates that happen to be present. Axes A, C and E (methods/standards named, splits declared, candidate-bound units) genuinely PASS on inspection: every kill/acceptance gate names a real standard (ASTM/ISO/EPA/SSPC/MIL), panel_plan/panel_counts/randomization/blocking are all declared, prediction_ledger binds all 3 declared candidates 1:1 with sha-bound lineage, and every per_candidate_measurements entry (14/14) carries an explicit unit field -- these are NOT invented failures. This is a genuine, targeted break of 2 of 5 required axes, not a rubber-stamp attack.
refutation_criterion_verbatim: The test plan lacks named methods and standards, pre-locked acceptance thresholds and kill criteria, declared splits, quantified uncertainty, or the candidate-bound unit-specified data-capture template.
